text:
luca: heads-up: during the long tail load run we instrumented yesterday, fragmentation slowly rose and correlated with a burst of tiny allocations from the metadata service. logging attached.
maya: saw that. after ~8h the host had ~30% slab internal slack and compact cycles spiked which impacted p99 a bit.
kevin: can we avoid compacting slabs that are dense with prefix cache lines? that seemed to cause a spike in cache misses after compaction.
sana: two orthogonal ideas: (A) slab_tainting: mark slabs that were recently compacted or that hold many prefixes and avoid returning them for small allocs for a TTL; (B) rewarm_governance: cap the rewarm activity and make it tenant-budgeted.
luca: sketch of slab_tainting semantics:
- on compact completion mark slab.taint_ts = now, slab.taint_reason = "post_compact"|"prefix_heavy"
- allocator fast-path avoids using tainted slabs for small-size-class allocations
- taint decays with an adaptive TTL (base 10s * hotness_factor)

maya: the adaptive TTL is key; TTL too long will starve pools, too short won't protect prefix cache. hotness_factor could be derived from recent access QPS to pages in that slab.
kevin: implementation question: do we store taint bits in slab header (fast) or in a side table (more flexible)? slab header would be fastest but increases metadata cost. side table allows GC of old entries.
sana: prefer slab header + versioned epoch so we can bump and scan cheaply. metadata overhead: 8-16 bytes per slab probably acceptable.
luca: rewarm_governance idea: runtime buys rewarm_tokens per-tenant from a shared meter. on first post-compact miss we can consume a small token amount and initiate async prefetch of neighbor cache-lines/pages. tokens refill at tenant-level rate proportional to footprint.
maya: combine with a 'prefetch_bandwidth_guard' per-host so we don't saturate NIC/PCIe during rewarm storms. track metrics: rewarm_attempts, rewarm_hits, rewarm_bandwidth_bytes.
kevin: agree. also add 'compact_affinity_score' for each slab computed as expected_frag_reduction / compact_cost. prefer high score slabs. compaction worker should pop best-scoring slabs given token budget.
sana: currency model recap:
- compaction tokens (allocator-owned): spent to run compaction work; bucket refills by footprint
- rewarm tokens (runtime-owned): spent to prefetch after compaction; budgeted per-tenant
- global bandwidth guard (host): prevents rewarm + compaction IO from exceeding safe thresholds

luca: corner cases:
- pinned ranges inside high-score slabs -> subtract pinned_fraction from expected_frag_reduction
- tenants with tiny footprints but high frag -> provide emergency token top-ups only when host frag exceeds watermark

maya: quick perf experiment plan:
1) baseline: existing global compaction waves every 30s
2) proto: slab_tainting + affinity scoring + compaction tokens (no rewarm)
3) full: add rewarm_governance + bandwidth guard
metrics: host_frag_ratio, tenant_frag_ratio, compact_cpu_seconds, rewarm_bandwidth, p95/p99 gen latency

kevin: operator tooling: add /debug/frag/top-slabs and a CSV export for slab scores so SREs can verify selection.
sana: security note: ensure tenant IDs are only used for accounting; no cross-tenant data moves during compaction. compaction only consolidates same-tenant or untagged slabs.
luca: action items:
- I'll draft an RFC for slab_tainting + slab header layout
- maya will implement the affinity scorer in the sim harness and run the three-step experiments
- kevin will add a minimal debug endpoint and the bandwidth guard prototype
- sana will design the token interfaces for allocator & runtime and write the small API spec

compaction-bot: snapshot saved: slab-tainting-rewarm-governance by luca at 1739991111
luca: target: staging canary in ~12 days if sims look good. thanks all.
